verdict: Erie Indemnity's revenue was nearly flat at $1.07 billion and net income held at $182 million, as higher agent commissions absorbed the growth in management fees.

segments.name: Management fees — policy issuance & renewal
segments.note: The fee Indemnity earns for issuing and renewing policies for the Erie Insurance Exchange — its main business.

segments.name: Administrative services reimbursement
segments.note: Money the Exchange pays back for claims handling and other administrative services — a pass-through matched dollar-for-dollar by the same cost below.

segments.name: Management fees — administrative services
segments.note: Fees for running claims, life insurance and investment services for the Exchange and its subsidiaries.

opex.name: Commissions
opex.note: What Indemnity pays the independent agents who sell Erie policies.

opex.name: Agent incentive compensation
opex.note: Extra pay for agents tied to premium growth and underwriting results.

opex.name: Non-commission expenses
opex.note: People, technology and underwriting support — the cost of running the operation.

otherDetail: Investment income of $19.9M (net investment income of $25.4M minus $5.5M of realized, unrealized and impairment losses) plus $5.5M of other income.
follow100Note: Investment and other income added $2.37 for every $100 of operating revenue, which is why the cost and profit slices add back to exactly $100.

takeaways.title: Core fees grew
takeaways.text: Management fees for policy issuance and renewal — the engine of the business — rose 2.6% to $847 million as the Exchange's direct written premiums grew 1.8%.

takeaways.title: Agents took a bigger share
takeaways.text: Commissions and agent incentives together rose about 5% to $485 million on incentive pay tied to better underwriting results, which is why operating income slipped 0.7% despite higher fees.

takeaways.title: EPS essentially flat
takeaways.text: Net income was $182.0 million, or $3.48 a share, versus $182.9 million and $3.50 a year ago; for the first nine months, net income is up 3.4% to $513 million.

footerNote: Erie Indemnity is the management company (attorney-in-fact) for the Erie Insurance Exchange; it does not itself underwrite insurance. Figures come from the earnings release and investor supplement, reported in $ thousands and shown here in $M. Administrative-services cost is treated as the direct cost of revenue because it is reimbursed dollar-for-dollar.
